judgements.reason: Every OrthogonalL2Bases target (hermiteHilbertBasis, prodHilbertBasis, chebyshevTHilbertBasis, weightL2Isometry) is already in Tau Ceti. AlgebraicCodingTheory still needs minimum distance and duals, weight enumerators with MacWilliams, Type II codes, the explicit Golay and hexacode computations, Construction A and the discriminant-module bridge.

Coding theory is shallow finite algebra (MacWilliams, Golay/hexacode verification, Construction A) over the completed integral-lattice library. Ado–Iwasawa must first get full PBW with U(L) a Noetherian domain, then stack nilradical and derivation theory, derivation-stable cofinite ideals, Levi decomposition with Weyl reducibility over non-closed fields, and the central p-polynomial/Krull route.

Ado–Iwasawa is a single algebraic programme (PBW, nilradical, Levi, central p-polynomials) over Mathlib's rich Lie theory. AlgebraicTopology must build excision, cellular homology, Eilenberg–Zilber/Künneth, the Serre and Cartan–Leray spectral sequences, cup/cap products with Poincaré duality and Hurewicz/Whitehead, and also consumes collars and a smooth triangulation theorem that are not built.

Diophantine needs long proofs (Roth, the subspace theorem, Baker/Matveev bounds, E/G-functions), but they sit on existing heights, Siegel's lemma and Liouville with few stacked layers. AlgebraicTopology needs a comparable amount of theory built as a deeper tower of new constructions (subdivision/excision → cellular homology → Eilenberg–Zilber and Serre spectral sequences → cup/cap products and Poincaré duality → Hurewicz/Whitehead) plus unbuilt geometric-topology inputs.

Diophantine's missing theorems (Roth, the subspace theorem, explicit linear forms in logarithms, Siegel–Shidlovskii) are deep but mostly long proofs on existing height theory. LieGroups needs the whole Ado–Iwasawa roadmap for Lie III plus absent geometric foundations (closed-subgroup and Frobenius theorems, quotient and complex manifolds for G/T and G_ℂ/B, a degree argument for torus conjugacy) before maximal tori, Weyl integration, Borel–Weil and KAK.

LieGroups needs Ado, Frobenius, maximal tori, complexification and Borel–Weil. QSeries needs half-integral weight and Jacobi forms, Rademacher's formula, harmonic Maass forms and Zwegers completions, plus quantum modular forms built on WRT invariants, a full moonshine proof (VOAs, no-ghost theorem, Monster Lie algebra) and part of ModularCurvesPartII, a much larger body.

ReductiveGroupsPartII needs the unbuilt structure and existence theory of reductive groups and Chevalley–Demazure schemes, then Bruhat–Tits buildings and parahorics. QSeries needs several independent large towers (metaplectic and Jacobi forms over adelic automorphic prerequisites that already import RG2.0a, harmonic Maass and mock theta theory, WRT invariants, and moonshine with VOAs and the Monster Lie algebra).

ReductiveGroupsPartII's gap is reductive structure and existence theory plus Bruhat–Tits buildings and parahorics. ModularCurvesPartII needs several foundations that are all absent (GAGA, algebraic stacks and coarse spaces, étale cohomology with Poincaré duality, Néron models and Jacobians) before its own compactified moduli, bad-fibre models, Hecke correspondences, Ihara's lemma and A_f.

PerfectoidSpaces must finish adic spaces and add adic étale geometry, almost mathematics, tilting, almost purity, diamonds D1–D4 and the prismatic inputs behind Q4. ModularCurvesPartII needs a somewhat larger set of absent foundations (GAGA, stacks and coarse spaces, étale duality and nearby cycles, abelian schemes, Néron models) plus twenty stages of its own moduli and Hecke theory.

PerfectoidSpaces is one foundational tower over adic spaces. SmallRamification's base-case table consumes Faltings–Shafarevich finiteness, Néron models, integral p-adic Hodge theory (whose period rings already pass through perfectoid tilts), ordinary modularity lifting over totally real fields and potential modularity.

DiamondEtaleCohomology needs perfectoid spaces, diamonds, enhanced derived sheaves and Huber's étale cohomology. SmallRamification needs Faltings finiteness, ordinary modularity lifting (Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms, Hida theory, deformation rings) and potential modularity, and its declared prerequisites for R25.5 even reach DiamondEtaleCohomology.

GrossZagier's stack contains the modularity machinery behind Heegner points (and, through its declared Jacquet–Langlands route, diamond étale cohomology) plus Shimura curves, theta and Waldspurger, Arakelov intersection theory and the Yuan–Zhang–Zhang formula. That is far beyond the perfectoid, diamond and derived-sheaf tower that DiamondEtaleCohomology needs.

IntegralIwasawaTheory needs p-adic zeta functions, the Wiles, Dasgupta–Kakde and Kurihara main conjectures and K-theory comparisons including the norm-residue theorem. GrossZagier needs all of SmallRamification's modularity stack (Faltings, modularity lifting, potential and Serre modularity) plus Shimura curves, the theta correspondence, arithmetic intersection theory and YZZ, a markedly larger missing body.

Both are near the top. IntegralIwasawaTheory adds Quillen and motivic K-theory with the norm-residue theorem and the Brumer–Stark and Kurihara main-conjecture machinery. SmallRamification's prerequisites (Faltings–Shafarevich finiteness, Hida-theoretic ordinary lifting, potential modularity, Shimura varieties and integral p-adic Hodge theory) form a broader missing stack.

OrthogonalL2Bases is fully realized in Tau Ceti (hermiteHilbertBasis, prodHilbertBasis, chebyshevTHilbertBasis). Ado–Iwasawa still needs full PBW, nilradical and derivation theory, Levi decomposition and the central p-polynomial/Krull argument.

PerfectoidSpaces is one foundational tower (adic geometry, almost purity, diamonds, prismatic inputs) that GrossZagier itself reaches through p-adic Hodge regulators. GrossZagier additionally needs modular and Shimura curves, automorphic theta theory, Arakelov heights, Heegner points with modularity, and YZZ.

AlgebraicTopology's gap is large, but it builds on Mathlib's singular homology, homological algebra and CW complexes. ReductiveGroupsPartII must first supply the unstarted structure, existence and Chevalley–Demazure layers of reductive group theory, then stack relative valued root data, buildings, parahoric group schemes and decompositions, which makes a deeper tower.

The two share étale duality, stacks, abelian schemes and enhanced derived sheaves. Beyond that, ModularCurvesPartII adds GAGA, Néron models and its own moduli and Hecke theory, whereas DiamondEtaleCohomology adds Huber's adic étale cohomology, perfectoid spaces with almost purity, diamonds and v-descent, prismatic inputs and ECD's four operations, a larger and deeper addition.

Diophantine's missing theorems (Roth, the subspace theorem, Baker bounds, E/G-functions) sit on existing heights and Siegel's lemma. QSeries needs metaplectic and Jacobi forms, harmonic Maass and mock theta theory, WRT invariants and a moonshine proof with VOAs and the Monster Lie algebra, plus pieces of ModularCurvesPartII.

Coding theory needs only finite-algebra layers over the completed lattice library. LieGroups needs the closed-subgroup and Frobenius theorems, Lie III via all of Ado–Iwasawa, maximal tori and Weyl integration, complexification, Borel–Weil and the KAK decomposition.

IntegralIwasawaTheory consumes ModularCurvesPartII itself (R12–R14.1, for Hilbert–Eisenstein p-adic interpolation). On top of that it needs p-adic L-functions, Iwasawa cohomology, the Wiles, Dasgupta–Kakde and Kurihara main conjectures, and K-theory with the norm-residue theorem.

GrossZagier's Heegner-point input needs elliptic-curve and Serre modularity, whose base cases are SmallRamification's table. So it contains SmallRamification's whole stack and adds Shimura-curve realizations, theta and Waldspurger, arithmetic intersection theory and the YZZ formula.

Diophantine's gaps (Roth, the subspace theorem, Baker bounds, E/G-functions) rest on existing heights. PerfectoidSpaces needs unfinished adic spaces, adic étale geometry, almost mathematics, tilting and almost purity, diamonds, enhanced derived sheaves and prismatic cohomology.

ReductiveGroupsPartII needs reductive structure theory plus Bruhat–Tits buildings and parahorics. DiamondEtaleCohomology needs perfectoid spaces, diamonds with v-descent, enhanced derived sheaves, and Huber and scheme étale duality before ECD's four operations, compactifications and constructibility.
